text:
sara: FYI customer ACME reported invoice shows ~45k tokens billed but our served_tokens logs show ~32k. They're asking for a breakdown. I'm attaching a minimal repro we ran on their workload.

matt: thanks — can you paste the sample request headers? specifically if they enabled continuous batching / prefetch or any custom routing.

sara: they use continuous batching with `x-continuous-batch: true` and enabled prefix caching for repeated prompts. Repro curl below:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \ 
 -H "x-continuous-batch: true" \ 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
 -d '{"model":"rw-13b","inputs":["Summarize: ...","Summarize: ..."],"prefix_cache":true}'
```

sara: runtime log snippet from our repro instance (masked):
```
[2026-05-14T10:12:01Z] request_id=REQ-1 incoming size=512
[2026-05-14T10:12:01Z] batch_id=BATCH-42 prefetch_keys=[k1,k2]
[2026-05-14T10:12:01Z] cache_hit=true prefix_hits=2 served_tokens=240 billed_tokens_emitted=360
[2026-05-14T10:12:01Z] request_id=REQ-2 incoming size=512
[2026-05-14T10:12:01Z] cache_hit=true prefix_hits=2 served_tokens=240 billed_tokens_emitted=360
```

matt: whoa — billed_tokens_emitted is higher than served_tokens in that trace. Looks like prefetch is doing accounting per-prefetch rather than deduping across requests in the same continuous batch.

oliver: that matches a bug we saw months ago where prefix cache accounting increments the metered token counter for each prefetch call, even when the same KV segment services multiple requests in a batch. The billing pipeline consumes those increments as separate token events.

anjali: if that's true we need a clear list of affected invoices and a recommended credit. Can we confirm whether invoiced tokens are strictly additive of those emitted counters? Also need customer invoice ids.

sara: customer invoice: INV-2026-04-9901 (April usage). They reported the spike on 2026-04-29. I verified our logging for that day and saw many BATCH-IDs with duplicate prefetch accounting spikes.

matt: quick theory: continuous batching prefetch issues a prefetch per request in the batch loop; runtime dedups at serve time for cache hits but the metering hook is called per-prefetch call. Two mitigations:
- short-term: change billing consumer to collapse identical prefetch token events by batch_id + cache_key within a 60s window
- medium-term: patch runtime to attach `metering_scope=batch_dedupe_id` when prefetch is initiated so billing service can dedupe immediately

oliver: patch is low-risk and can be rolled to a canary. I'll open PR with a feature flag `metering.prefetch_dedupe=true` and push to dedicated canary tomorrow.

anjali: for customer-facing action we can issue a pro-rated credit for the delta (billed - served). Can you produce a CSV of affected batch_ids and delta per invoice? We need that to generate the credit note.

sara: running a quick query now — sample output:
```
invoice, batch_id, billed_tokens, served_tokens, delta
INV-2026-04-9901, BATCH-324, 480, 320, 160
INV-2026-04-9901, BATCH-418, 720, 480, 240
INV-2026-04-9901, BATCH-987, 360, 240, 120
```

anjali: perfect. please attach the CSV to the ticket and I'll start the credit workflow. Also need a note for finance describing this as "metering duplication due to prefetch per-request accounting in continuous batching".

matt: follow-up engineering note: we should also audit other metering hooks that run inside loops (kernel selection, kv prefetch, warm-up tokens). If any of them call the billing counter per-loop-iteration we risk similar double-counting for high-fanout batches.

oliver: agreed. adding audit items to the runtime backlog. I'll link PR and the canary build in this thread when ready.

kev-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/engine-runtime v1.12.3-metric-fix -> 2026-05-15T02:00:00Z (ETA 30m). :rocket:

sara: customer updated: they're good with a credit and want the technical explanation in writing. I'll draft a short postmortem for them once we confirm PR and the exact credit amount.

anjali: once we have final delta CSV, I'll route the credit. tagging @finance to expect a manual credit for INV-2026-04-9901.

matt: final dev action: we'll add `batch_id` to all metering events and add a dedupe window in billing consumer. That will cover both prefetch and warmup cases. Also add unit tests to simulate 10x fanout batches.

sara: thanks team — keeping this thread open until the canary deploy finishes and invoice credit is issued. :v:
